label: Claude Opus 5.5
output:
Subject: Re: Our plan for next year

Appa, Amma, Kiran, Divya, everyone,

Sorry for the slow reply. I've just come off a run of nights and only properly sat down with all of this today.

First, I'm so happy you're coming. I've been grinning about it since Appa's email. The kids are beside themselves. Anika has already made a laminated welcome timetable, and one of the entries is "Paati teaches us rasam, Tuesdays," so Amma, I'm afraid you've been booked.

Kiran, you're right that you should have been asked, and you should have heard it from me well before an email on a Saturday morning. To be honest about how it happened: the idea came from Appa, on a phone call back in August when Rohan was showing him the vegetable patch on video and he said "I could grow drumsticks there." It went from there. I started the visa paperwork because the agent needed my sponsor letter and bank statements, and that was the point where I should have rung you. I didn't, and that's on me. I'm sorry.

You've put your concerns clearly, so here's where things stand on each one.

**1. Appa's heart.** This is the one I've thought about most, and you're right that visitors aren't covered by the NHS for free. So:

- I've got a travel insurance quote with pre-existing cardiac cover. It's about £640 each for the six months, and the agent has confirmed it covers the stent. I'm happy to send you the policy wording so you can check it yourself before we commit.
- Dr. Prakash has agreed to do Appa's review in March, before they fly. He'll also do a video consult in July, halfway through, and he's happy to share his notes with me. So the doctor who knows Appa's case stays involved the whole time.
- The annexe at the back is finished. It's all on the ground floor with no steps, and it has its own shower with a grab rail.
- Leicester Royal is fifteen minutes from the house, and I know a lot of the cardiology team there.

None of that means nothing can go wrong. But if something did happen, I think he'd be well looked after. If you think I've missed anything, tell me and I'll sort it out.

**2. Amma being away so long.** This is a fair point, and I hadn't given it enough weight. Six months is a long time, and you know better than anyone how she's been since Paati. The return ticket is flexible, so if Amma wants to go home after six weeks, or two months, or whenever, she can. Nobody will think it's a failure. April to September is the outer limit, not a commitment.

**3. Ganesh Chaturthi.** I don't want you and Divya to lose that. There are a couple of ways we could do it:

- Amma and Appa fly from here to Pune for Ganesh Chaturthi in September and finish the trip with you, then go home to Bangalore from there.
- Or all of you come here in August. If you'd like that, I'd love to cover your flights. Please take me up on it. It would be wonderful to have everyone here at once, and Divya's murukku achu might finally get some use in my kitchen.

We could also do both. I'm happy with whatever suits you.

I think this deserves a proper conversation rather than more emails, so can we do a family video call this Sunday at 4pm UK time, which is 9.30pm in India? Appa and Amma, that's after your dinner. Kiran, if that time doesn't work after your travelling, suggest another and we'll fit around you.

I want this to be something we've all agreed on, not something that was decided and then announced. Kiran, I'm grateful you said all this plainly. It's the kind of thing I'd want someone to ask if the plan were the other way round.

Love to everyone,
Meera
